module.purpose: Provides selectors, matchers, extraction helpers, status calculations, and timing statistics for inspecting RTK Query state and actions in the Redux DevTools monitor.
module.summary: This utility module identifies RTK Query API slices, extracts cached queries and mutations, calculates cache and subscription tallies, reconstructs request lifecycles from lifted Redux actions, and formats timing statistics. It also supports selection lookup, provided-tag inspection across RTK Query schema versions, query status flags, endpoint matching, and filtering actions associated with a selected resource.
module.businessContext: Supports developer observability for applications using RTK Query. Failure would impair API cache inspection, request timing analysis, tag visibility, and selected-query action tracing in Redux DevTools.

detail.name: computeRtkQueryRequests
detail.signature: function computeRtkQueryRequests(type: 'queries' | 'mutations', api: RtkQueryApiState, sortedActions: AnyAction[], currentStateIndex: SelectorsSource<unknown>['currentStateIndex']): Readonly<Record<string, RtkRequest>>
preconditions: api contains the reducer state and configuration required for the selected request type.
sortedActions is ordered consistently with currentStateIndex.
Matching actions expose meta.requestId and meta.requestStatus.
postconditions: Returns a record keyed by request ID for matching actions processed through index currentStateIndex, inclusive.
Each created request record contains queryKey, requestId, endpointName, and status.
The final matching request status is reflected for each request ID.
Pending actions with numeric startedTimeStamp preserve that timestamp.
Fulfilled actions with numeric fulfilledTimeStamp preserve that timestamp.
A missing action start timestamp may be filled from api[type][request.queryKey].startedTimeStamp when the cached value is numeric.
invariants: Only actions accepted by the matcher for the selected type and api reducer path contribute to the result.
Actions after currentStateIndex are not processed.
Requests are grouped by action.meta.requestId.
The first action for a request determines its initial query key and endpoint name; subsequent matching actions update the existing record.
The returned request map is constructed locally and does not mutate the supplied api or sortedActions values.
edgeCases: When sortedActions is empty or currentStateIndex is below the first action index, no actions are processed.
When a matching action has no string arg.queryCacheKey, its request ID is used as queryKey.
When a matching action has no arg.endpointName, endpointName is '-'.
When multiple matching actions share a request ID, one record is returned and its status reflects the last processed action.
When a fulfilled request has no numeric startedTimeStamp on its actions, a numeric cached startedTimeStamp is used if available.
Non-matching actions and matching actions after currentStateIndex are ignored.
stateMutations: Mutates only the locally allocated requestById map and its request records while computing the return value.
detail.summary: Builds request records for matching RTK Query query or mutation actions up to the supplied current state index. It tracks request identity, endpoint, status, and available request timestamps, including a cache-based start timestamp fallback.

Fallback endpointName when an action does not provide arg.endpointName.

preconditions: queryCacheEntries is iterable and each entry contains a query cache key and query cache value.
requestById is a mutable object used as the request record map.
postconditions: Returns the requestById object.
Each eligible cache entry with numeric startedTimeStamp and fulfilledTimeStamp contributes a record keyed by its derived requestId.

Added records contain queryKey, requestId, endpointName, startedTimeStamp, fulfilledTimeStamp, and status.
invariants: For type equal to "queries", requestId is the cache entry's requestId or an empty string when absent.

detail.name: computeQueryApiTimings
preconditions: requestById is a record whose values are RtkRequest objects.
postconditions: Returns a QueryTimings value derived from all request values in requestById.
Completed requests are evaluated using their fulfilledTimeStamp values.
Request duration comparisons are based on the request timestamps available on each RtkRequest.
invariants: The input requestById is not mutated.
The computation examines each request value at most once during aggregation.
Requests without numeric fulfilledTimeStamp values are not eligible for completed-request recency selection.
edgeCases: An empty requestById produces timing aggregates with no selected request candidates.
Requests with non-numeric fulfilledTimeStamp values are treated as not fulfilled for recency aggregation.
When no completed request is available, the latest and oldest completed-request candidates remain unset.
Duration extrema are initialized so that the first eligible duration can establish the slowest and fastest candidates.
detail.summary: Computes aggregate timing information for the requests in a query request map, including relative request recency and duration-based timing categories.

specLiterals.role: Initial boundary for selecting the latest fulfilled request and the slowest duration.
Initial upper boundary for selecting the oldest fulfilled request and the fastest duration.

units.name: computeApiTimings

detail.name: computeApiTimings
preconditions: The input contains request records with fulfillment timestamps; requests may or may not have numeric start timestamps.
postconditions: Completed requests with numeric start timestamps no later than their fulfillment timestamps contribute their fulfillment-minus-start duration to the aggregate timing statistics.
The returned timing information reflects the oldest fulfilled request and, when durations are available, the fastest, slowest, and average pending durations.
invariants: A pending duration is included only when startedTimeStamp is numeric and startedTimeStamp <= fulfilledTimeStamp.
The pending duration is calculated as fulfilledTimeStamp - startedTimeStamp.
The fastest duration is updated only for a duration smaller than the current fastest duration.
The slowest duration is updated only for a duration greater than the current slowest duration.
edgeCases: Requests without a numeric startedTimeStamp do not contribute to pendingDurations.
Requests whose startedTimeStamp is later than fulfilledTimeStamp do not contribute to pendingDurations.
When no valid pending durations exist, the average is not computed from a duration sample.
A request with a fulfillment timestamp earlier than the current oldest fulfillment timestamp becomes the oldest request.
stateMutations: Mutates local timing accumulators and request references while computing the result; no external state mutation is established.
detail.summary: Computes aggregate timing information for API requests, including request age and completed request durations. It identifies the oldest request and the fastest and slowest requests with valid start and fulfillment timestamps.
